title: Grade 6 Place Value: Thousandths to Billions
seo_title: Grade 6 Place Value Worksheets: Thousandths to Billions, Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Small to large numbers (thousandths to billions)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on place value from thousandths to billions for the BC curriculum: millions and billions, reading and writing BC and Canada populations, decimals to thousandths, comparing and ordering, and rounding in real life. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Every place is worth 10 times the place to its right, from thousandths all the way up to billions.
key_sub: A billion is 1000 millions (1 000 000 000). Compare decimals place by place, not by length: 0.5 = 0.50 > 0.45. To round, look one place to the right: 5 or more rounds up.
body_html:
Place value to billions

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. Big numbers are split into groups of three digits called periods: billions, millions, thousands and ones. In Canada we leave a small space between the groups (5 000 879), not a comma. A 4-digit number has no space (4536).

NameDigitsZeros
one thousand10003
one million = 1000 thousands1 000 0006
one billion = 1000 millions1 000 000 0009

Read and write large numbers

Read one group at a time, from the left, and say the group’s name. Write every group with three digits, using 0 for empty places.

Words to digits

At the 2021 census, British Columbia had five million eight hundred seventy-nine people. Write the number in digits.

Five million → 5. No thousands → 000. Eight hundred seventy-nine → 879.

Answer: 5 000 879

Millions with a decimal

Write 2.6 million in digits.

0.1 million = 100 000, so 0.6 million = 600 000. 2 000 000 + 600 000.

Answer: 2 600 000

Decimals to thousandths

After the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths. 1 hundredth split into 10 equal parts makes 10 thousandths. Read the word “and” as the decimal point.

Compare and order

Whole numbers: count the digits first. A 10-digit number is greater than any 9-digit number. If they have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left.

Decimals: compare the whole numbers first. Then give the decimals the same number of places by adding zeros at the end, and compare tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

Example

Order 0.5, 0.45 and 0.405 from least to greatest.

Write 0.500, 0.450 and 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths.

Answer: 0.405, 0.45, 0.5

Rounding

  1. Find the place you are rounding to.
  2. Look at the digit one place to its right.
  3. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down.
  4. Whole numbers: change the digits after that place to 0. Decimals: drop the digits after that place.
RoundLook atAnswer
36 991 981 to the nearest millionthe hundred thousands digit: 937 000 000
2 642 825 to the nearest hundred thousandthe ten thousands digit: 42 600 000
4.68 to the nearest tenththe hundredths digit: 84.7
1.879 to the nearest hundredththe thousandths digit: 91.88

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up millions and billions (8 billion → 8 000 000)A billion is 1000 millions: 8 billion = 8 000 000 000
0.45 > 0.5 because it has more digitsUse the same number of places: 0.45 < 0.50
Missing a zero group (five million eight hundred seventy-nine → 5879)Write each group as three digits: 5 | 000 | 879
Giving the digit, not its value (the 3 in 36 991 981 is 3)It is in the ten millions place: 30 000 000
Cutting off instead of rounding (4.68 → 4.6)Look at the next digit: 8, so round up to 4.7
Rounding twice (48.346 → 48.35 → 48.4)Round the number you started with: 48.3

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about numbers in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: The Grade 6 Number standard is “small to large numbers (thousandths to billions)”. Students read, write, compare, order and round whole numbers up to billions and decimals to thousandths.

faq.q: How many millions are in a billion?
faq.a: There are 1000 millions in one billion. One million is 1 000 000 (6 zeros) and one billion is 1 000 000 000 (9 zeros).
0.5 is bigger. Write both with the same number of places, 0.45 and 0.50, and compare the tenths: 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths.

faq.q: Why do BC students write 5 000 879 with spaces instead of commas?
faq.a: Canada uses the SI style in math: numbers with 5 or more digits are split into groups of three with a small space, and 4-digit numbers have no space (4536). This avoids mix-ups with the decimal comma used in French.

items.q: Which number is one billion?
items.e: One billion is 1000 millions. It has 9 zeros in three groups: 1 000 000 000. 1 000 000 is only one million.

items.q: How many zeros does one billion have when you write it in digits?
items.e: One billion = 1 000 000 000: three groups of three zeros, so 9 zeros. One million has 6 zeros.

items.q: How many millions are there in one billion?
items.e: 1 000 000 000 ÷ 1 000 000 = 1000. Each period is 1000 times the period before it: 1000 thousands make a million, and 1000 millions make a billion.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the millions place, so it is worth 7 millions = 7 000 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the billions place, so it is worth 3 billions = 3 000 000 000. The digit is 3, but its value is 3 000 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the hundred millions place, so it is worth 6 hundred millions = 600 000 000. The digit is 6, but its value is 600 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the ten millions place, so it is worth 4 ten millions = 40 000 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 40 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 4 hundred thousands = 400 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 400 000.

items.q: In 1 426 839 075, which digit is in the millions place?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: ones, thousands, millions, billions. In 1 426 839 075 the millions digit is 6, worth 6 000 000.

items.q: In 3 915 460 287, which digit is in the ten millions place?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: ones, thousands, millions, billions. In 3 915 460 287 the ten millions digit is 1, worth 10 000 000.

items.q: Which number has a 4 in the hundred millions place?
items.e: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, …, millions, ten millions, hundred millions. In 2 408 135 769 the 4 is the first digit of the millions group, worth 400 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 3 620 784 159?
items.e: The 6 is in the hundred millions place, so it is worth 6 hundred millions = 600 000 000. The digit is 6, but its value is 600 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 493 286 501?
items.e: The 9 is in the ten millions place, so it is worth 9 ten millions = 90 000 000. The digit is 9, but its value is 90 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 5 867 140 923?
items.e: The 7 is in the millions place, so it is worth 7 millions = 7 000 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 2 106 795 483?
items.e: The 2 is in the billions place, so it is worth 2 billions = 2 000 000 000. The digit is 2, but its value is 2 000 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 6 027 450 000?
items.e: 6 027 450 000 has 10 digits. The 6 is in the fourth group from the right, the billions group. It is worth 6 billion = 6 000 000 000.

items.q: In 770 000 000, the first 7 is worth how many times the second 7?
items.e: The first 7 is worth 700 000 000. The second 7 is worth 70 000 000. 700 000 000 ÷ 70 000 000 = 10. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

items.q: What is 10 times 50 000 000?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place to the left: 5 ten millions become 5 hundred millions. 10 × 50 000 000 = 500 000 000.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 3 000 000 000 + 40 000 000 + 500 000 + 200 + 7 = 3 040 500 207.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 800 000 000 + 6 000 000 + 9000 + 30 = 806 009 030.

items.q: At the 2021 census, the city of Vancouver had six hundred sixty-two thousand two hundred forty-eight people. Which number is this?
items.e: Six hundred sixty-two thousand → 662 in the thousands group. Two hundred forty-eight → 248. So 662 | 248 = 662 248.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Kamloops had ninety-seven thousand nine hundred two people. Which number is this?
items.e: Ninety-seven thousand → 97. Nine hundred two → 902 (no tens, so write 0). So 97 | 902 = 97 902.

items.q: At the 2021 census, British Columbia had five million eight hundred seventy-nine people. Which number is this?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Five million → 5. No thousands → 000. Eight hundred seventy-nine → 879. So 5 | 000 | 879 = 5 000 879. The empty thousands group still needs three zeros.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Surrey had 568 322 people. How do you read this number?
c: five hundred sixty-eight three hundred twenty-two
five hundred sixty-eight million three hundred twenty-two
five hundred sixty-eight thousand three hundred twenty-two
items.e: Split 568 322 into groups of three: 568 | 322. Read the first group and say “thousand”, then read the second group: five hundred sixty-eight thousand three hundred twenty-two.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Prince George had 76 708 people. How do you read this number?
c: seven hundred sixty thousand seven hundred eight
items.e: 76 708 = 76 | 708. Seventy-six thousand, then seven hundred eight. The 0 means there are no tens, so you do not say a tens word.

items.q: Terry Fox grew up in Port Coquitlam, BC. At the 2021 census, Port Coquitlam had sixty-one thousand four hundred ninety-eight people. Which number is this?
items.e: Sixty-one thousand → 61. Four hundred ninety-eight → 498. So 61 | 498 = 61 498.

items.q: Which number is three billion?
items.e: A billion has 9 zeros. 3 billion = 3 000 000 000 (10 digits). 3 000 000 is 3 million: a million is 1000 times smaller than a billion.

items.q: How do you read 1 000 000 000?
items.e: 1 000 000 000 has four groups: 1 | 000 | 000 | 000. The fourth group from the right is billions, so it is one billion.

items.q: In 2023, Canada’s population passed 40 million. Which number is 40 million?
items.e: 40 million = 40 × 1 000 000 = 40 000 000. Write 40 in the millions group, then two groups of 000. 40 000 000 000 would be 40 billion.

items.q: There are about 8 billion people in the world. Which number is 8 billion?
items.e: One billion is 1000 millions: 1 000 000 000. So 8 billion = 8 000 000 000, with 8 in the billions group and three groups of 000 after it. 8 000 000 is only 8 million.

items.q: Which number is twelve million five thousand?
items.e: Twelve million → 12. Five thousand → 005 in the thousands group. No ones → 000. So 12 | 005 | 000 = 12 005 000.

items.q: Which number is two billion forty million?
items.e: Two billion → 2. Forty million → 040 (write the 0 to fill the hundred millions place). No thousands and no ones → 000 | 000. So 2 | 040 | 000 | 000 = 2 040 000 000.

items.q: How do you read 4 050 300 000?
c: four million fifty thousand three hundred
four billion five hundred million three hundred thousand
four billion fifty million three thousand
four billion fifty million three hundred thousand
items.e: Groups: 4 | 050 | 300 | 000. That is 4 billion, 50 million and 300 thousand: four billion fifty million three hundred thousand.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Canada had 36 991 981 people. How do you read this number?
c: thirty-six million nine hundred ninety-one thousand nine hundred eighty-one
thirty-six billion nine hundred ninety-one million nine hundred eighty-one thousand
three hundred sixty-nine million nine hundred nineteen thousand eighty-one
items.e: Split 36 991 981 into groups from the right: 36 | 991 | 981. That is 36 million, 991 thousand and 981: thirty-six million nine hundred ninety-one thousand nine hundred eighty-one.

items.q: Canada’s area is nine million nine hundred eighty-four thousand six hundred seventy square kilometres. Which number is this?
items.e: Nine million → 9. Nine hundred eighty-four thousand → 984. Six hundred seventy → 670. So 9 | 984 | 670 = 9 984 670 km².

items.q: In 36 991 981 (Canada’s population in 2021), what is the value of the digit 3?
items.e: 36 | 991 | 981: the 3 is in the ten millions place, so it is worth 3 ten millions = 30 000 000.

items.q: Which shows 5 000 879 in expanded form?
items.e: 5 000 879 has 5 millions, 0 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 8 hundreds, 7 tens and 9 ones: 5 000 000 + 800 + 70 + 9.

items.q: A news story says that Metro Vancouver has about 2.6 million people. Which number is 2.6 million?
items.e: 2.6 million = 2 millions and 6 tenths of a million. One tenth of a million is 100 000, so 6 tenths is 600 000. 2 000 000 + 600 000 = 2 600 000.

items.q: A music video has been watched 1.5 billion times. Which number is 1.5 billion?
items.e: 1.5 billion = 1 billion and 5 tenths of a billion. 5 tenths of a billion is 500 million. 1 000 000 000 + 500 000 000 = 1 500 000 000.

items.q: Write 4 300 000 as a number of millions.
What is the value of the red digit in 5.208?
items.e: The red 8 is the third digit after the decimal point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 8 thousandths = 0.008. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 7.063?
items.e: The red 6 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 6 hundredths = 0.06.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 24.719?
items.e: The red 7 is the first digit after the decimal point, in the tenths place. Its value is 7 tenths = 0.7.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 9.142?
items.e: 9 . 1 4 2: the 4 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths place. It is worth 4 hundredths = 0.04.

items.q: In which place is the digit 9 in 0.059?
items.e: 0 . 0 5 9: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. The 9 is in the thousandths place.

items.q: In 6.381, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: After the decimal point the places are tenths (3), hundredths (8) and thousandths (1). So the hundredths digit is 8.

items.q: In 32.604, which digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: After the decimal point: tenths 6, hundredths 0, thousandths 4. The thousandths digit is 4.

items.q: Which number is equal to 0.3?
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 0.3 = 0.30 = 0.300. 0.03 and 0.003 have the 3 in a different place.

items.q: Write 7 ones, 3 hundredths and 2 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 7 . 0 3 2 = 7.032. 7.32 would have 3 tenths.
2 ones, 6 tenths, 5 hundredths and 9 thousandths: 2 . 6 5 9 = 2.659.

items.q: Which shows 8.247 in expanded form?
items.e: 8 ones, 2 tenths, 4 hundredths and 7 thousandths: 8 + 0.2 + 0.04 + 0.007.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.6?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 6 tenths = 600 thousandths. 0.6 = 0.600.

items.q: Write 0.087 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.087 has three decimal places, so it is thousandths: 87 thousandths = 871000. 87100 would be 0.87.

items.q: Which number is six and thirty-four thousandths?
items.e: “And” stands for the decimal point. Thirty-four thousandths must end in the third place after the point: 6.034. 6.34 would be thirty-four hundredths.

items.q: How do you read 0.508 in words?
items.e: 0.508 has three decimal places, so read the digits as a whole number and say “thousandths”: five hundred eight thousandths.

items.q: In 4.44, the 4 in the tenths place is worth how many times the 4 in the hundredths place?
items.e: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. 0.4 = 10 × 0.04. So the answer is 10.

items.q: What number is 0.001 more than 2.709?
items.e: 9 thousandths + 1 thousandth = 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth. So 2.709 + 0.001 = 2.710 = 2.71. 2.719 adds 1 hundredth, not 1 thousandth.

items.q: What number is 0.01 more than 3.395?
items.e: Add 1 hundredth: 9 hundredths + 1 hundredth = 10 hundredths = 1 tenth. So 3.395 + 0.01 = 3.405. 3.396 adds only 1 thousandth.

items.q: What number is 0.1 less than 6.07?
items.e: Take away 1 tenth. 6.07 has 0 tenths, so regroup 1 one as 10 tenths: 6.07 − 0.1 = 5.97. 6.06 takes away 1 hundredth.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1 and 6 once to make the greatest number with 1 digit before the decimal point and 3 digits after it.
items.e: Put the largest digit in the ones place, then the next largest in the tenths, hundredths and thousandths places: 8.631. 1.368 is the least number you can make.

sets.title: Compare and order large numbers and decimals

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 2 040 000 000 has 10 digits and 980 000 000 has only 9, so 2 040 000 000 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which is greater: 2 billion or 900 million?
items.e: 2 billion = 2 000 000 000 (10 digits). 900 million = 900 000 000 (9 digits). A billion is 1000 millions, so 2 billion is much greater, even though 900 > 2.

items.q: Compare 0.45 and 0.5.
items.e: 0.5 = 0.50. Compare the tenths: 4 tenths < 5 tenths. So 0.45 < 0.5. More digits does not mean a greater number.

items.q: Compare 0.7 and 0.69.
items.e: 0.7 = 0.70. Compare the tenths: 7 > 6. So 0.7 > 0.69.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 9 ten thousands is more than 1 ten thousand. So 36 991 981 > 36 919 981.

items.q: Compare 5.06 and 5.060.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 5.06 = 5.060.

items.q: Compare 0.004 and 0.04.
items.e: 0.04 = 0.040. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 4. So 0.004 < 0.04. 4 thousandths is less than 4 hundredths.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 987 654 321 has only 9 digits, so it is the least, even though it starts with 9. The other three have 10 digits and the same billions digit. Compare the hundred millions: all 0. Compare the ten millions: 1 020 000 000 has 2, the others have 0. So 1 020 000 000 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: All have 7 digits. Millions, hundred thousands and ten thousands are the same in 5 000 879 and 5 000 978, and both have 0 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 8 < 9. 5 008 790 and 5 080 790 have more thousands. So 5 000 879 is the least.

items.q: Compare 0.215 and 0.22.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0.215 and 0.220. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 1 < 2. So 0.215 < 0.22. Do not compare 215 with 22.

items.q: Compare 3.9 and 3.899.
items.e: 3.9 = 3.900. The ones are the same. Compare the tenths: 9 > 8. So 3.9 > 3.899.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.800, 0.790, 0.799, 0.087. Compare the tenths first: only 0.8 has 8 tenths. So 0.8 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.506, 0.560, 0.600, 0.650. The least is 0.506, even though it has the most digits.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Vancouver had 662 248 people, Surrey had 568 322 and Burnaby had 249 125. Order the populations from least to greatest.
items.e: All three have 6 digits. Compare the hundred thousands: 2 < 5 < 6. So the order is 249 125, 568 322, 662 248.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 0.5, 0.45, 0.405
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths. So 0.405, 0.45, 0.5.

items.q: Order from greatest to least: 6.4, 6.38, 6.405, 6.04
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 6.400, 6.380, 6.405, 6.040. Greatest first: 6.405, 6.4, 6.38, 6.04.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1 000 000 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100 000 000 (one hundred million), not 10 000 000. The arrow is 1 space after 500 000 000: 600 000 000.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 2.3 to 2.31 there are 10 equal spaces. 2.31 − 2.30 = 0.01, so each space is 1 thousandth, not 1 hundredth. Count 6 spaces on from 2.300: 2.306.

items.q: 4☐3 000 000 > 457 000 000. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred millions are the same (4). Compare the ten millions: the box must be 5 or more. If it is 5, compare the millions: 3 < 7, so 453 000 000 is too small. 463 000 000 > 457 000 000.

items.q: Which number is between 0.4 and 0.5?
items.e: 0.4 = 0.400 and 0.5 = 0.500. 0.409 is between them. 0.049 and 0.399 are less than 0.4, and 0.51 is more than 0.5.

items.q: A coho salmon caught on the Fraser River has a mass of 4.68 kg. What is its mass to the nearest tenth of a kilogram?
items.e: 4.68 is between 4.6 and 4.7. Look at the hundredths digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 4.7. 4.6 kg just cuts off the 8. Answer: 4.7 kg.

items.q: At the 2021 census, the city of Vancouver had 662 248 people. What is this rounded to the nearest thousand?
items.e: 662 248 is between 662 000 and 663 000. Look at the hundreds digit, one place to the right of the thousands: 2. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 662 000 people.

items.q: Arjun ran 5.38 km in the Terry Fox Run. What is this distance to the nearest whole kilometre?
items.e: 5.38 is between 5 and 6. Look at the tenths digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down to 5. 5.4 km is the nearest tenth, not the nearest whole number. Answer: 5 km.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Surrey had 568 322 people. What is this rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: 568 322 is between 560 000 and 570 000. Look at the thousands digit, one place to the right of the ten thousands: 8. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 570 000 people.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Kelowna had 144 576 people. What is this rounded to the nearest thousand?
items.e: 144 576 is between 144 000 and 145 000. Look at the hundreds digit, one place to the right of the thousands: 5. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 145 000 people.

items.q: Gas in Kamloops costs $1.879 per litre. What is this price to the nearest cent (hundredth of a dollar)?
items.e: 1.879 is between 1.87 and 1.88. Look at the thousandths digit: 9. 5 or more, so round up to 1.88. A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, so keep two decimal places. Answer: $1.88.

items.q: At the 2021 census, British Columbia had 5 000 879 people. What is this rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
items.e: 5 000 879 is between 5 000 000 and 5 100 000. Look at the ten thousands digit, one place to the right of the hundred thousands: 0. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 5 000 000 people.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Nanaimo had 99 863 people. What is this rounded to the nearest thousand?
items.e: 99 863 is between 99 000 and 100 000. Look at the hundreds digit, one place to the right of the thousands: 8. 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Regroup them as 1 ten thousand. 99 thousands + 1 thousand = 100 thousands. Answer: 100 000 people.

items.q: On a rainy day in Vancouver, 12.95 mm of rain fell. What is this to the nearest tenth of a millimetre?
items.e: 12.95 is between 12.9 and 13.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 one, so 12.9 becomes 13.0. Do not write 12.10. Answer: 13.0 mm.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Canada had 36 991 981 people. What is this rounded to the nearest million?
items.e: 36 991 981 is between 36 000 000 and 37 000 000. Look at the hundred thousands digit, one place to the right of the millions: 9. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 37 000 000 people (37 million).

items.q: A box of Okanagan cherries has a mass of 2.496 kg. What is this to the nearest hundredth of a kilogram?
items.e: 2.496 is between 2.49 and 2.50. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. 9 hundredths + 1 hundredth = 10 hundredths = 1 tenth, so 2.49 becomes 2.50. Answer: 2.50 kg.

items.q: On average, Earth is 149 597 871 km from the Sun. What is this distance rounded to the nearest million kilometres?
items.e: 149 597 871 is between 149 000 000 and 150 000 000. Look at the hundred thousands digit, one place to the right of the millions: 5. 5 or more, so round up. The millions digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 millions. Regroup them as 1 ten million. Answer: 150 000 000 km (150 million km).

items.q: At the 2021 census, Metro Vancouver had 2 642 825 people. What is this rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
items.e: 2 642 825 is between 2 600 000 and 2 700 000. Look at the ten thousands digit, one place to the right of the hundred thousands: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Keep the 6 in the hundred thousands place and write zeros after it. Answer: 2 600 000 people.

items.q: Simran jumped 3.475 m in the long jump at a track meet in Burnaby. What is this to the nearest hundredth of a metre?
items.e: 3.475 is exactly halfway between 3.47 and 3.48. A number that is exactly halfway rounds up. Answer: 3.48 m.

items.q: A news report says that about 250 000 people lived in Burnaby in 2021. The number was rounded to the nearest ten thousand. Which could be the real population?
items.e: Numbers from 245 000 to 254 999 round to 250 000. 249 125 is in that range. 255 000 and 258 300 round up to 260 000, and 244 800 rounds down to 240 000.

items.q: Four swimmers raced 50 m at a swim meet in Victoria. Which time does not round to 36.5 s to the nearest tenth?
items.e: Times from 36.45 s up to (but not including) 36.55 s round to 36.5 s. 36.44 has 4 hundredths, so it rounds down to 36.4 s.

items.q: Chloe’s snowboard race time at Whistler, rounded to the nearest tenth, is 52.3 seconds. Which could be her real time?
items.e: Times from 52.25 s to 52.34 s round to 52.3 s. 52.26 s is in that range. 52.36 s and 52.35 s round up to 52.4 s, and 52.21 s rounds down to 52.2 s.

items.q: The number of people who rode a ferry route in one year, rounded to the nearest hundred thousand, is 1 500 000. What is the least the real number could be?
items.e: Numbers from 1 450 000 to 1 549 999 round to 1 500 000. 1 449 999 would round down to 1 400 000, so the least is 1 450 000. (1 549 999 is the greatest.)

items.q: Owen’s 100 m time, rounded to the nearest tenth, is 12.7 s. The real time was measured to the hundredth. What is the least it could be?
items.e: Times from 12.65 s to 12.74 s round to 12.7 s. 12.64 s would round down to 12.6 s, so the least is 12.65 s. (12.74 s is the greatest.)

items.q: Kai’s ski race time on Grouse Mountain was 48.346 s. He rounded it to the nearest hundredth (48.35 s), then rounded that to the nearest tenth and got 48.4 s. What is 48.346 s rounded to the nearest tenth?
items.e: Always round the number you started with. 48.346 is between 48.3 and 48.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 48.3 s. Rounding twice gives the wrong answer.
